subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the equation of the line passing through the point of intersection of 2x+3y=1, 3x+4y=6 and perpendicular to the line 5x−2y=7.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1B (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.62 — SAQ chapter 9 The Straight Line, answer 56.2. No appearance years are printed against this answer. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — no [N Marks] tags are printed against this answer. It is not a bare guess: the SAME CHAPTER prints 1+1+2 on answer 59 (book p.63), and this answer is cut to the same shape — the two setting-up moves at one mark each and the closing work at two. Where an answer's own shape is four equal moves instead, 1+1+1+1 is used and this note says so. Paper position: Maths-1B Section B runs Q11-Q17 at 4 marks each, answer any 5 of 7. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. NOTE: The Straight Line is the FIRST Maths-1B unit to occupy ALL THREE sections of the paper — the book's IPE Blue Print (book p.3) gives it 2+2 marks in Section A, 4 in Section B and 7 in Section C, 15 in all, tying Differentiation as the highest-scoring unit on the paper. It therefore has three separate chapters in this book: LAQ chapter 1 (book pp.14-18), SAQ chapter 9 (pp.61-64) and VSAQ chapter 14 (pp.79-82). All three boundaries were walked: p.19 opens Pair of Straight Lines, p.65 opens Limits & Continuity, and p.83 opens 3-D Coordinates. The book's separate STAR QUESTIONS PLUS bank (pp.104-108) contributes three more, answers 182-184, authored here as sqp1-sqp3.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say how you get the slope, and how you get a point on the line.

steps.label: Find the required slope
steps.margin_note: First mark. The new line is perpendicular to a given line, so its slope is fixed before any point is known. Read the given slope off the coefficients as −a/b, then flip and negate it.
steps.memory_tip: PERPENDICULAR means flip and negate the given slope, before any point is known.

recall.must_convey: That the slope of the given line is found as −a/b and the required slope is −1/m, because the lines are perpendicular.
accept: perpendicular so take minus one over the given slope
read the slope as minus a over b then flip and negate
the required slope is minus one by m

steps.why: Slope comes first because it needs only the OTHER line, not the point — and the point takes more work.
common_mistakes: Using the same slope, which would give a parallel line instead.

steps.label: Solve for the point
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The new line passes through the meeting point of two OTHER lines, so solve that pair. This half is independent of the slope work above.
steps.memory_tip: Solve the other pair for the point — independent of the slope work.

recall.must_convey: That the two lines are solved together to find the point the required line passes through.
accept: solve the two given lines to find their point of intersection
use cross multiplication on the pair
the required line passes through this point

steps.why: The question gives the line's direction one way and its position another, and the two are found independently before being combined.
common_mistakes: Solving the wrong pair of lines.

steps.label: Write the point-slope form
steps.margin_note: Third mark. With a point and a slope, the point-slope form y − y₁ = m(x − x₁) writes the line in one line.
steps.memory_tip: y − y₁ = m(x − x₁) with the point and slope just found.

steps.why: A point and a slope determine a line uniquely, which is why the two independent halves are enough between them.
common_mistakes: Using the slope-intercept form and having to find c separately.
Swapping x₁ and y₁ in the formula.

steps.label: Simplify to the line
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Clear the fractions and collect into ax + by + c = 0 form.
steps.memory_tip: Clear fractions and collect into ax + by + c = 0.

recall.must_convey: That clearing fractions and collecting gives 2x + 5y + 17 = 0.

steps.why: The board expects the answer in ax + by + c = 0 form, so the tidy-up is worth its own mark.
common_mistakes: Leaving fractions in the final answer.
Sign slip when multiplying through by a denominator.

insider_note: Take the slope from the third line first: 5/2 inverts to −2/5. The cross-multiplication denominator is −1, so both coordinates change sign, and that is where P(14, −9) is usually lost.
